The pass left two counts unchecked, that generator 1 moves 3,094 pieces and that generators 1 and 45 move disjoint slots; the integrator counted both with core.py on the model (c152350f), and The mathematician's scoped re-check of 23 November 2026 confirmed both, recounted on the shipped assets. The mathematician's check of the human-test sheet on 25 November 2026 found that step 5, the end state is the base, rests on the certificate statement through the preview leaf, not on kernel:receipt(Base), which is the revision the run read; the step map now says so. specification.function: preview_word(w) proposes the word w, as the solver named it, to the command layer's `operation.preview` row and returns the fixed acknowledgement {base, id}. The solver sees the layer's preview of w: the kernel's complete effect of w at the base revision.
specification.inputs: w: a literal word of the generators 1 to 1200, each letter signed (a negative letter is the inverse), as the solver named it

parameters.none: the entry has no parameter beyond its inputs

budget.none: the entry sets no budget of its own: a run is bounded by the run limits of the job that runs it (KN7.7)

specification.output: record {base, id}: the revision the run read and the proposal's ID. The preview's outcome is withheld from the program (BND.11) and shown to the solver by the shell.

menu.none: 600-cell-Full has no menu: its 1,200 generators are the model's

specification.domain: every literal word of the 1,200 generators at any revision of a 600-cell-Full session

tie_rule.none: the entry chooses nothing: it proposes the one word it was given

empty_answer.none: the acknowledgement is never empty; the empty word is refused by the layer (KN2's recipe shape), the program still receives the fixed acknowledgement, and the shell shows the refusal: an empty answer never says that a word does nothing

negative_scope.none: the entry answers no yes-or-no question, so it has no negative answer

specification.outside_scope: The certificate covers the model's 1,200 generators and their inverses. A word whose preview the layer refuses (the empty word, a word under a protected orbit it would move) is outside it: the program's answer is still the fixed acknowledgement, and the meaning is the layer's refusal, which the shell shows.

justification.text: Each generator is a permutation of the 259,800 sticker slots, and the negative letter names the inverse permutation (the generator convention of the model manifest), so the composite of a generator and its inverse moves no sticker.

reason.statement: a generator followed by its inverse is the identity permutation of the 259,800 sticker slots
reason.idea: A twist followed by the same twist undone leaves every piece where it was, so the preview of a generator and then its inverse shows no change: no piece moves, no orbit is touched and the end state is the base.

failure.hypothesis: the second letter is the inverse of the first
failure.outcome: without it the end state is in general not the base: generator 1 alone moves 3,094 pieces in the kernel's effect row (read from the effect of the word [1])

by_hand.not_meant: The preview shows the effect of the one word the solver named. It does not say that the word is useful, short or part of a solution, and the tool never proposes a word of its own.

steps.check: The entry proposes w = [1, -1] as given: its body is one proposal of its parameter.
The word has two letters and each letter is one generator, so its expansion has 2 primitive moves.
-1 names the inverse of generator 1, so the word applies generator 1 and then undoes it: the composite is the identity, and 0 pieces move.
An orbit gets a support row only when a piece of it moves; no piece moves, so there are 0 rows.
The end state is the base state under the identity: the base state itself.

leaf_specs.spec: The layer previews the proposed literal word at the base revision: the kernel's complete effect of the word, withheld from the program and shown to the solver.
The receipt's base is the revision the run read.
The receipt's id is the run's proposal ID `<run>/1`.
